method: Identical update-500 optimizer recovery, full-history batches, frozen recipe and training code. Discard ten warmup updates, measure forty fixed updates, profile one separate final update. Both attempts succeeded without nonfinite updates or checkpoint writes.

findings.interpretation: H100 clearly improves wall time in this test. Its 12.5% cost reduction versus today's L40S allocation is not a robust fleet-wide cost claim: relative to the earlier L40S same-window rate, H100 is 5.5% more expensive. Historical comparison is sensitivity only, not a new primary endpoint.

observed: Backward CUDA interval improves from 1.448s to 0.439s (3.30x), forward from 1.384s to 0.866s (1.60x), optimizer from 0.147s to 0.108s (1.36x). These intervals include launch gaps, not only kernel execution.
Both warm windows have about 11 microseconds exposed input wait per update; transfers are 6-8 milliseconds. Bulk input waiting is not the observed steady-state limit.
Separate traces contain about 21600 kernels per update, with median duration about 2.4 microseconds on both GPUs.

Name-based device-kernel classification assigns about 24-25% of summed kernel duration to matrix multiplies, 48-49% to elementwise work, 7-9% to reductions, and 7-8% to copies. Fused Triton kernels remain unclassified; these are not wall-time fractions.

Instrumented GPU active-union time falls from 2.427s to 0.758s (3.20x), while end-to-end warm throughput improves 2.10x. Instrumented idle share is 16.5% on L40S and 30.9% on H100, not a steady-state utilization or MFU estimate.
source_facts: The current and one selected future board each go through the 15-layer BT4 encoder; only the last future layer is trainable. BT4 and state-projector activations are recomputed during backward to save memory.

The policy-bearing BT4 remains eager for numerical compatibility. Fresh projector/DFM/JEPA regions are compiled. Eager normalizations, casts, adds, multiplies and reductions introduce many distinct kernels.

JEPA predicts eight states sequentially and the Muon/AdamW optimizer has repeated small operations. Sequential structure and launch costs do not scale with tensor-core peak FLOPS. The profile does not establish JEPA as the dominant cost.
workload_diagnosis.inference: The workload is mixed, not a pure tensor-core GEMM benchmark. Faster device math and memory operations help substantially, while dispatch, smaller operations and dependencies increasingly limit scaling. Memory traffic is a plausible mechanism, but no hardware bandwidth/occupancy counters were collected to prove saturation. Near-zero exposed input wait also does not exclude CPU preprocessing contention with kernel dispatch.
workload_diagnosis.profiling_limit: Each trace is a separate final update with instrumentation and no following-batch prefetch; do not substitute its timing for the preregistered warm-window result.
candidate_next_tests_not_launched: Matched prefetch scheduling/CPU-preparation ablation to separate dispatch contention from GPU execution.
Numerically checked fusion of eager BT4 normalization/casts or launch reduction. Earlier whole-BT4 compilation failed parity, so do not enable it silently.
Use available memory to evaluate reduced rematerialization only under an explicit matched numerical/performance protocol.

epoch_decision.decision: Do not launch the epoch or raise budget. Even the H100 train-loop estimate alone exceeds the outer budget. Remaining original history data also needs preparation; replaying the 553-update subset is not an original-data epoch. Recommend a bounded runtime-optimization pass, or obtain a new budget after staging estimates.

retention: No models or optimizer states were written by GPU-001. Raw traces and telemetry remain hash-bound on chess-dfm-training-results under benchmarks/gpu001-2ca0e018960c56266a25; compact results and profiles are committed. Existing checkpoints and data were not deleted.
verification: All 10 trainer artifacts per GPU downloaded and SHA256/size verified; primary summary recomputed from metrics; seven targeted analysis/benchmark tests passed; Modal container inventory empty after both results returned.
limits: One container per GPU and forty warmed updates; no fleet-level confidence interval.

Same source, data and optimizer state does not imply bitwise equality across BF16 hardware kernels. First losses are 7.847913 and 7.847539; later numerical trajectories drift. No playing-strength or gradient-direction parity conclusion follows.
